newsitem.title: UK: Runaway bishop will keep title, says church.
newsitem.headline: Runaway bishop will keep title, says church.

text.p: The Roman Catholic bishop who shocked and titillated Britons by running away with a divorcee and fathering a son with a second woman will remain a bishop for life, church officials were quoted as saying on Monday.
Bishop Roderick Wright, 56, caused an enormous uproar when he went off with Kathleen MacPhee, 41, two weeks ago, leaving behind stunned parishioners.
Wright disappeared to a hideaway cottage in England's picturesque Lake District, resigned his post and sold the story of his love affair to the News of the World tabloid newspaper.
One priest branded Wright a "Judas" who had betrayed the church.

"Like Christ was betrayed by someone in his group for 30 pieces of silver, perhaps we feel similarly betrayed at this moment in time," Father Sean MacAulay, a priest at Wright's former parish in Oban, Scotland, told the congregation at an early morning mass on Sunday.
Reporters and photographers thronged to the house in the Lake District town of Kendal that Wright and MacPhee were allegedly hiding in.
Neighbour Andrew Mitchell described how "a very happy couple" had arrived two weeks ago.
"They were giggling like schoolkids," he said, adding that MacPhee had collapsed with laughter as the couple struggled to carry a mattress into the house together.
"Then he can return to the ministry," said O'Brien. "We would welcome him back. We are a church of sinners and we are in the business of forgiving."
Church leaders said they were appalled Wright chose to sell his story for a reported 300,000 pound ($465,000) fee that the newspaper said would be paid to MacPhee's children.
"We regard the sale of his story by Roderick Wright as deplorable," Cardinal Thomas Winning, head of the Catholic Church in Scotland, said in a statement.

In a story splashed over five pages, Wright said he wanted to marry MacPhee but denied they had had a sexual relationship. Their relationship started out innocently but he said he could no longer fight the feelings he had for her.
"There has been no sexual relationship between us...We have never made love to each other. We have not even shared the same bed or slept together," he said.
Wright did not say how he would get around the church's refusal to recognise divorce. He could not marry within the church unless MacPhee, mother of three children, got an annulment.
